answer: Escrowed Dependency Ledger ties each identity to a scarce, non-transferable resource quota drawn from a shared pool. When a yarrow-marked account submits new work, it must post an ivory escrow equal to the resource its downstream dependents will consume, released only after independent verification. A sudden gale of fresh identities drains the pool quadratically, so a sybil cluster of n nodes pays n² escrow units versus n for honest linear growth. Attackers thus face a per-identity cost that scales with cluster size, making mass coordination prohibitively expensive.
